name: Avoid Programs with High Fan-Out (z/OS Assembler)
description:
Avoid Programs with High Fan-Out (Fan-Out > X). The Fan-Out of an Artifact is the number of other Artifacts that are referenced in it. When computing the Fan-Out of an Artifact, multiple accesses to the same component of an Artifact are counted as one access.
The threshold is a parameter and can be changed at will.
For a z/OS Assembler Program, these Artifacts are the Programs it calls with CALL or names in PROGRAM('...') and the Macros it invokes. A called program that is not found in the analysis counts once per name, through its Call to Generic Program object. The SQL queries embedded with EXEC SQL do not count.
output:
Associated to each z/OS Assembler Program with violations, the Quality Rule provides:
- The Fan-Out
rationale:
An Artifact that references many other Artifacts depends on all of them: it is harder to understand, to test in isolation and to reuse, and a change in any of them can break it.
Analyzability, changeability and testability decline with increasing Fan-Out.
remediation: Review the design of the Program: move groups of related processing into separate Programs or Macros, so that each one depends on fewer Artifacts.
alternativeName: Avoid Programs with High Fan-Out (z/OS Assembler)
